## Architectures

<a id="ar-omni"></a>

### AR-Omni

Single 7B-parameter autoregressive Transformer decoder, initialized from the Anole interleaved image-text model, that generates text, images and speech from a shared joint vocabulary via a scene-aware VQ image tokenizer and discrete speech/text tokenizers, without separate per-modality expert components.

AR-Omni is a unified autoregressive model for 'omni' multimodal understanding and generation, handling text, image and speech within one Transformer decoder and shared token vocabulary rather than routing modalities to separate expert modules. Initialized from the Anole interleaved image-text model and extended to speech, it addresses modality imbalance with task-aware loss reweighting, improves visual quality with a perceptual alignment loss, and manages the stability-creativity trade-off in generation with finite-state decoding. The paper reports strong performance across text, image and speech tasks while keeping real-time capability, including a 0.88 real-time factor for speech generation.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.17761) · [GitHub](https://github.com/ModalityDance/AR-Omni) · [Project](https://modalitydance.github.io/AR-Omni/)

![AR-Omni — Figure 1](../assets/architectures/ar-omni.png)

*Figure 1 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.17761)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I, A → T, I, A · **Interaction:** generation

Paper Figure 1: text, speech and image inputs are tokenized by a discrete multimodal tokenizer (images via a scene-aware VQ tokenizer producing a causal 1D sequence) into one joint vocabulary consumed by a single autoregressive Unified Decoder using residual-post-norm (swin-norm); a matching multimodal detokenizer reconstructs each modality's output. Training initializes from Anole (7B) and proceeds through multimodal pretraining (weighted next-token-prediction plus perceptual loss) followed by instruction fine-tuning. The project page linked from the paper and the ModalityDance/AR-Omni README (which links the arXiv paper) point to released AR-Omni-Pretrain-v0.1 and AR-Omni-Chat-v0.1 checkpoints on Hugging Face. Speech input is used for ASR (Table 5) and image input for captioning.

**License:** code: MIT.

</details>

<a id="arm"></a>

### ARM

7B autoregressive multimodal transformer initialized from Qwen2.5-7B, predicting a discrete Finite Scalar Quantization visual vocabulary built on a frozen SigLIP2-SO400M encoder, with images reconstructed by a latent diffusion decoder initialized from FLUX.1-dev and reinforcement learning used to align unified understanding, text-to-image generation and editing.

ARM unifies image understanding, text-to-image generation and instruction-based editing within one next-token-prediction framework built around a discrete semantic visual tokenizer. The tokenizer projects frozen SigLIP2 features through Finite Scalar Quantization into a 65K-token discrete codebook, trained jointly with caption, pixel-reconstruction, contrastive and feature-distillation losses so the tokens carry both semantic and low-level information; a FLUX.1-dev-initialized latent diffusion decoder reconstructs pixels from the tokens. A 7B autoregressive transformer initialized from Qwen2.5-7B, with an added linear head for visual-token prediction, is pretrained on 2.5T multimodal tokens and then optimized with reinforcement learning, which the authors report substantially improves text-to-image and editing metrics (WISE score 0.50 to 0.56) and induces cross-task synergy between the two.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11188) · [GitHub](https://github.com/wdrink/ARM)

![ARM — Figure 2](../assets/architectures/arm.png)

*Figure 2 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11188)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → T, I · **Interaction:** editing

Paper Figure 2 shows the unified discrete visual tokenizer. Trained on 2.2B internal image-text pairs for the tokenizer and 2.5T multimodal tokens for the language model. The abstract gives https://github.com/wdrink/ARM as the project page; no license is stated in the repository. Understanding results include MMMU 40.2 and POPE 87.3.

</details>

<a id="bagel"></a>

### BAGEL

Decoder-only Mixture-of-Transformers (Qwen2.5 initialized) with an understanding expert for text and SigLIP2 tokens and a generation expert that denoises FLUX VAE latents by rectified flow, sharing self-attention in every layer.

BAGEL (Scalable Generative Cognitive Model) is ByteDance Seed's open unified model for multimodal understanding and generation, with 7B active and 14B total parameters. One decoder-only transformer, split into an understanding expert and a generation expert that attend to the same interleaved token sequence, predicts text by next-token prediction and images by rectified flow over VAE latents. It is pretrained on trillions of tokens of text, image-text pairs and interleaved web and video data, and the paper reports text-to-image results on GenEval and WISE, image editing on GEdit-Bench and an intelligent-editing benchmark, and optional reasoning (thinking) before generation or editing.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.14683) · [GitHub](https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/Bagel) · [Model card](https://huggingface.co/ByteDance-Seed/BAGEL-7B-MoT)

![BAGEL — Figure 2](../assets/architectures/bagel.png)

*Figure 2 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.14683)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → T, I · **Interaction:** editing

Both experts are full copies of the Qwen2.5 LLM with hard routing: the generation expert processes only VAE tokens; the understanding expert handles text and ViT tokens (paper Figure 2). Understanding uses a SigLIP2-so400m/14 encoder with NaViT-style native aspect ratios and an MLP connector; generation uses the frozen FLUX VAE (8x downsampling, 16 channels) with 2x2 patch embedding, and the timestep embedding is added to the VAE token states instead of AdaLN. A generalized causal attention lets later tokens attend to clean VAE and ViT tokens of earlier images; interleaved multi-image generation uses diffusion forcing. The paper also shows qualitative multi-frame generation and world-navigation examples, which are not listed as a video modality here.

**License:** code: Apache-2.0; weights: Apache-2.0.

**Variants:** BAGEL-7B-MoT.

</details>

<a id="blip3-o"></a>

### BLIP3-o

Frozen Qwen2.5-VL backbone whose learnable query outputs condition a Lumina-Next-style diffusion transformer that generates CLIP image features by flow matching, followed by a diffusion-based decoder to pixels.

BLIP3-o is an open family of unified multimodal models from Salesforce Research and collaborators that adds image generation to a frozen Qwen2.5-VL understanding model. Instead of generating VAE latents, a diffusion transformer generates semantically rich CLIP image features conditioned on the language model's outputs, and a diffusion decoder turns those features into an image. The paper compares CLIP and VAE targets with MSE and flow-matching objectives, argues for sequential training (understanding first, then generation), and releases code, weights, pretraining captions and the BLIP3o-60k instruction-tuning set.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.09568) · [GitHub](https://github.com/JiuhaiChen/BLIP3o) · [Model card](https://huggingface.co/BLIP3o/BLIP3o-Model-8B)

![BLIP3-o — Figure 1](../assets/architectures/blip3-o.png)

*Figure 1 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.09568)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → T, I · **Interaction:** generation

Learnable query vectors appended to the prompt are processed by the autoregressive backbone; their outputs condition the DiT, which denoises 64 fixed-length CLIP embeddings; a second, diffusion-based visual decoder reconstructs the image from those embeddings (paper Section 3.3 and Figure 1). The backbone is frozen, so understanding performance is that of Qwen2.5-VL; the 8B model trains about 1.4B parameters. The 8B model uses Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and adds 30 million proprietary images to about 25 million open images; the 4B model uses Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct and open data only. The DiT follows Lumina-Next (3D RoPE, sandwich normalization, grouped-query attention). The released 8B checkpoint on Hugging Face is stated to be trained on open-source data only. Image editing is described as future work in this paper. The later BLIP3o-NEXT has its own card.

**License:** weights: Apache-2.0.

**Variants:** BLIP3o-Model-8B; BLIP3o-Model-4B.

</details>

<a id="chameleon"></a>

### Chameleon

Early-fusion decoder-only transformer that autoregressively models interleaved text tokens and discrete VQ image tokens in one vocabulary.

Chameleon is Meta FAIR's family of early-fusion, token-based mixed-modal models. Images are quantized into discrete tokens that share a single vocabulary with text, so one autoregressive transformer trained from scratch on interleaved image-text data can read and write arbitrary sequences of text and images, including text-to-image generation, captioning, visual question answering and long-form mixed-modal documents. The paper documents image generation, but the publicly released 7B and 34B checkpoints were published without image generation: Meta's release announcement states that the image generation model was not released and that the released models produce text-only output.

[Paper 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.09818) · [GitHub 1](https://github.com/facebookresearch/chameleon) · [Announcement](https://ai.meta.com/blog/meta-fair-research-new-releases/) · [Paper 2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.06135) · [GitHub 2](https://github.com/GAIR-NLP/anole)

![Chameleon — Figure 1 (PDF p. 2)](../assets/architectures/chameleon.png)

*Figure 1 (PDF p. 2) · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.09818)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → T, I · **Interaction:** generation

The image tokenizer (based on Make-A-Scene's tokenizer) encodes a 512×512 image into 1024 discrete tokens from an 8192-entry codebook; these codes are part of a 65,536-entry BPE vocabulary shared with text, and an image de-tokenizer decodes generated image tokens (paper Figure 1). Stable training at scale relies on query-key normalization, dropout and z-loss for the 7B model and on a revised layer-norm placement for the 34B model. The public release (7B and 34B) accepts mixed-modal inputs but produces text only; the research-only license applies to code and weights. Anole (GAIR, arXiv 2407.06135) is a third-party fine-tune of the released Chameleon 7B checkpoint that restores image and interleaved image-text generation by fine-tuning fewer than 40M parameters on about 6,000 samples; its weights follow the Chameleon license.

**License:** code: Chameleon Research License; weights: Chameleon Research License.

**Variants:** Chameleon-7B; Chameleon-34B; Anole-7b-v0.1 (GAIR fine-tune enabling image generation).

</details>

<a id="cm3"></a>

### CM3

Decoder-only transformer trained with a causally masked language modeling objective over minimal-HTML documents, where images referenced by <img> tags are quantized with a VQGAN into discrete tokens embedded inline as text.

CM3 (Causally-Masked Multimodal Modeling), from Meta AI, extends structured-document pretraining to full HTML documents including images and hyperlinks. Every <img> tag's image is resized and tokenized into discrete VQGAN codes that are inserted as text into the tag's src attribute, so a single decoder-only transformer trained purely with next-token prediction over document structure can later be prompted, zero-shot, to generate an image for a caption by producing an <img src=...> tag whose predicted tokens are decoded back to pixels.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.07520) · GitHub: no author-linked repository found

![CM3 — Figure 1 (PDF p. 3)](../assets/architectures/cm3.png)

*Figure 1 (PDF p. 3) · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.07520)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → T, I · **Interaction:** generation

Training data is Common Crawl News and English Wikipedia HTML, stripped to minimal-HTML (Section 3.1); each image is resized to 256x256 with random cropping and tokenized with the VQGAN from Esser et al. 2021 into 256 tokens per image, inserted as the img src value. The causally masked objective reorders a masked span to the end of the sequence so a left-to-right decoder can still learn to fill it in, illustrated against plain masked and causal language modeling (Figure 1, PDF p. 3). Section 3 covers CM3-Large and CM3-Medium/XL, with unconditional image generation and zero-shot image infilling demonstrated (Figures 3-4) via prompt engineering rather than a dedicated text-to-image objective. No official code or weight release was found.

**Variants:** CM3-Medium; CM3-Large; CM3-XL.

</details>

<a id="codi"></a>

### CoDi

Composable Diffusion: separately pretrained per-modality latent diffusion UNets (text, image, video, audio) whose conditioning encoders are aligned into a shared space, then bridged with cross-attention so any subset can be denoised jointly and synchronously from any combination of input modalities.

CoDi (Composable Diffusion), from the University of North Carolina and Microsoft Azure Cognitive Services Research, is an any-to-any generative model that produces any combination of text, image, video and audio outputs from any combination of input modalities in a single generation pass, including modality pairs never seen jointly in training. It starts from individually pretrained latent diffusion models per modality, aligns their conditioning encoders in a shared 'bridging alignment' space, and then couples the modality-specific UNets with cross-modal attention so that, for example, a text prompt can drive synchronized video-plus-audio generation or joint image-text-audio generation.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.11846) · [GitHub](https://github.com/microsoft/i-Code)

![CoDi — Figure 2](../assets/architectures/codi.png)

*Figure 2 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.11846)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I, V, A → T, I, V, A · **Interaction:** generation

Stage 1 trains each modality's diffusion model with a text-aligned prompt encoder via bridging alignment; Stage 2 freezes these UNets and adds cross-attention 'environment encoders' plus a latent-alignment step so the vision and audio (or other) UNets' predicted latents interact at each diffusion step, enabling synchronized joint generation (Figure 2). Single-to-single (e.g. text-to-image), multi-input and joint multi-output generation are all demonstrated (Figures 3-5). Video and audio are within scope for CoDi as a unified model, with text-to-image generation as one of its documented single-modality outputs. Code and the released checkpoint are MIT licensed.

**License:** code: MIT; weights: MIT.

</details>

<a id="cosmos3"></a>

### Cosmos 3

Mixture-of-Transformers initialized from a VLM (Qwen3-VL for Nano and Super): an autoregressive reasoner tower for text and ViT tokens and a diffusion generator tower that denoises Wan2.2 VAE latents by flow matching, joined by shared attention in every layer.

Cosmos 3 is NVIDIA's family of omnimodal world models for Physical AI, which jointly process and generate language, images, video, audio and robot or vehicle actions in one Mixture-of-Transformers model. Text is produced by next-token prediction in a reasoner tower, while images, video, audio and actions are produced by iterative denoising in a generator tower that attends to the reasoner's context. Text-to-image is one of its generation modes, and NVIDIA released Cosmos3-Super-Text2Image, a 64B checkpoint specialized for text-to-image by two-stage fine-tuning, which the technical report describes as ranked first among open-weight models on the Artificial Analysis text-to-image leaderboard at the time of writing.

[Model card](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Cosmos3-Super-Text2Image) · [Paper 1](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/cosmos-lab/cosmos3/technical-report.pdf) · [GitHub](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cosmos) · [Paper 2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.02800)

![Cosmos 3 — Figure 5 (PDF p. 11)](../assets/architectures/cosmos3.png)

*Figure 5 (PDF p. 11) · [Source](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/cosmos-lab/cosmos3/technical-report.pdf)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I, V → T, I, V, A · **Interaction:** generation

Each decoder layer has two parameter sets (reasoner and generator), both initialized from the same pretrained VLM; reasoner tokens attend causally only to the autoregressive subsequence, while generator tokens attend bidirectionally to both subsequences (technical report Figure 5, Section 2.3). Understanding uses a jointly trained ViT; generation uses the frozen Wan2.2-TI2V-5B video VAE (4x temporal and 32x32 spatial compression including a 2x2 patch merge), a frozen audio VAE and a unified action representation; positions use a 3D MRoPE with absolute temporal indexing. In text-to-image mode the noisy image tokens follow the text prefix, and images are treated as single-frame videos. Sizes: Edge 4B (not yet released), Nano 16B (8B dense base) and Super 64B (32B dense base). Text-to-image specialization fine-tunes Cosmos3-Super for 20k steps and then 2k steps on 470k curated pairs above 720p. Modalities listed are those of the family per the model card (video input may carry audio; action inputs and outputs are not modality codes here); the Text2Image checkpoint itself maps text to images. The source date is the release date stated on the model card; the technical report is dated 2026-06-22.

**License:** code: OpenMDW-1.1; weights: OpenMDW-1.1.

**Variants:** Cosmos3-Super-Text2Image; Cosmos3-Super-Text2Image-4Step; Cosmos3-Super; Cosmos3-Nano.

</details>

<a id="dreamllm"></a>

### DreamLLM

Vicuna-7B causal multimodal LLM with a CLIP-Large visual encoder that emits a <dream> token and learnable dream queries whose outputs condition a frozen Stable Diffusion U-Net through a linear projection.

DreamLLM, from Xi'an Jiaotong University, MEGVII, Tsinghua and others, is a learning framework for multimodal LLMs that both comprehend and create images and interleaved documents. Instead of forcing the LLM's outputs to match CLIP embeddings, it appends a set of learnable dream queries whose LLM outputs are projected into the conditioning space of a frozen Stable Diffusion decoder, which is trained through score distillation in pixel space. A special <dream> token lets the model decide where images go within text, so interleaved generative pretraining on web documents yields free-form interleaved image-text generation as well as text-to-image synthesis and visual understanding.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.11499) · [GitHub](https://github.com/RunpeiDong/DreamLLM)

![DreamLLM — Figure 2](../assets/architectures/dreamllm.png)

*Figure 2 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.11499)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → T, I · **Interaction:** generation

Images are encoded by OpenAI CLIP-Large with a linear projection; the condition projector to the SD U-Net is also linear, and the SD model stays frozen. The paper finds 64 dream queries best and reports an MS-COCO zero-shot FID of 8.46 for DreamLLM-7B. Training proceeds through alignment, interleaved generative pretraining (I-GPT) and supervised fine-tuning. Released checkpoints on Hugging Face: dreamllm-7b-chat-v1.0 and dreamllm-7b-chat-aesthetic-v1.0; no weight license was established.

**License:** code: Apache-2.0.

**Variants:** dreamllm-7b-chat-v1.0; dreamllm-7b-chat-aesthetic-v1.0.

</details>

<a id="duogen"></a>

### DuoGen

Interleaved multimodal system combining a Qwen2.5-VL-7B MLLM, which autoregressively decides when to emit a <Begin-of-Vision> token, with a diffusion transformer initialized from the Cosmos Predict 2.5 video-generation model that renders each image conditioned on MLLM hidden states and prior image latents.

DuoGen (NVIDIA) is a unified system for interleaved text-and-image generation: producing multi-step, multi-image sequences such as illustrated how-to instructions rather than a single image per prompt. A pretrained multimodal LLM (Qwen2.5-VL-7B) reads the conversation and previously generated images and decides, token by token, whether to keep writing text or trigger image synthesis; when it does, a diffusion transformer initialized from a video-generation model (Cosmos Predict 2.5) renders the next image conditioned on the MLLM's hidden states and on all prior images in the sequence, stacked as VAE latents along a temporal axis. The paper argues that a video-pretrained backbone gives better cross-image visual consistency than an image-only DiT, and trains the system in two stages that first teach the MLLM when to generate images and then align the connector and DiT to the MLLM on large-scale image/video transition data.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.00508) · [Project](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/dir/duogen/) · GitHub: no author-linked repository found

![DuoGen — Figure 3](../assets/architectures/duogen.png)

*Figure 3 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.00508)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → T, I · **Interaction:** editing

Stage 1 (instruction tuning) trains only the MLLM on 298k multimodal conversations converted from websites and synthetic prompts; Stage 2 (interleaved context alignment) freezes the MLLM and trains the connector and DiT on multi-modal alignment data including video-transition captions from 5M videos plus image generation/editing datasets. The connector projects MLLM hidden states of all tokens preceding the <Begin-of-Vision> token into the DiT's language-conditioning interface; classifier-free guidance drops the trailing text segment for the negative branch. Reported outputs are documented at 768x768 resolution. Code and data are stated to be released on the project page, but no repository link was found at review time.

</details>

<a id="emu-baai"></a>

### Emu (BAAI)

LLaMA-13B multimodal model that classifies next text tokens and regresses next continuous visual embeddings (EVA-CLIP features compressed by a Causal Transformer), decoded to images by a Stable Diffusion-initialized latent diffusion decoder.

Emu is BAAI's generative multimodal foundation model trained with one autoregressive objective over interleaved image, text and video data. Images are encoded by EVA-CLIP and compressed by a Causal Transformer into a fixed number of visual embeddings that sit alongside text tokens in a LLaMA sequence; the model is trained to classify the next text token or regress the next visual embedding. Generated visual embeddings condition a latent diffusion decoder, initialized from Stable Diffusion, that renders the image. The same model performs captioning, image and video question answering, in-context image-to-text and text-to-image generation. It is unrelated to Meta's Emu text-to-image model.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.05222) · [GitHub](https://github.com/baaivision/Emu)

![Emu (BAAI) — Figure 2](../assets/architectures/emu-baai.png)

*Figure 2 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.05222)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I, V → T, I · **Interaction:** generation

Videos are encoded as T frames × N visual embeddings, and pretraining data includes image-text pairs, interleaved webpages and interleaved video-text data. The Causal Transformer blocks use causal self-attention plus cross-attention to EVA-CLIP features. The visual decoder follows Stable Diffusion v1.5 settings, with new linear projections in the cross-attention modules to accept Emu's embeddings. Emu-I is an instruction-tuned version trained with LoRA on the frozen model. The repository is Apache-2.0; the Emu1 README states that the released weights (Emu w/ Decoder, Emu-I) are subject to LLaMA-1's license, so no separate weight license name is recorded. Emu2 is a separate card.

**License:** code: Apache-2.0.

**Variants:** Emu w/ Decoder (pretrained); Emu-I (instruction-tuned).

</details>

<a id="emu2"></a>

### Emu2

37B generative multimodal model (LLaMA-33B initialized) that regresses continuous EVA-02-CLIP visual embeddings alongside next-token text prediction, with an SDXL-initialized diffusion visual decoder.

Emu2 is BAAI's 37-billion-parameter successor to Emu, trained with a unified predict-the-next-multimodal-element objective over text, image-text pairs and interleaved image-text-video sequences. Each image is encoded by EVA-02-CLIP and pooled into 64 continuous visual embeddings interleaved with text tokens; the model classifies text tokens and regresses visual embeddings, which an SDXL-initialized diffusion decoder turns back into images. Unlike Emu, the visual decoder is trained as a stand-alone detokenizer without the language model. Instruction tuning yields Emu2-Chat for multimodal dialogue and Emu2-Gen, which accepts mixes of text, locations and images for text-to-image, grounded, subject-driven generation and editing.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.13286) · [GitHub](https://github.com/baaivision/Emu) · [Model card](https://huggingface.co/BAAI/Emu2-Gen)

![Emu2 — Figure 2](../assets/architectures/emu2.png)

*Figure 2 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.13286)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I, V → T, I · **Interaction:** editing

Visual Encoder, Multimodal Modeling and Visual Decoder are initialized from EVA-02-CLIP-E-plus, LLaMA-33B and SDXL-base; each image is mean-pooled to 8×8 patches (N = 64 embeddings). The Visual Decoder is trained on image autoencoding with the encoder and SDXL VAE frozen and only the U-Net updated. The paper also trains a separate video decoder (initialized from Stable Diffusion 2.1) conditioned on Emu2 embeddings; video output is not listed as a modality here. Emu2-Gen training data include grounded image-text pairs, InstructPix2Pix editing data and text-to-image data. The README lists the model license as a non-commercial license, initialized from LLaMA; no named license is recorded.

**License:** code: Apache-2.0.

**Variants:** Emu2 (pretrained); Emu2-Chat; Emu2-Gen.

</details>

<a id="emu3"></a>

### Emu3

Decoder-only transformer (Llama-style, 8B) trained from scratch with next-token prediction over text tokens and discrete image/video tokens from a MoVQGAN-based vision tokenizer.

Emu3 is BAAI's suite of multimodal models trained solely with next-token prediction. Images, videos and text are all tokenized into a discrete space, and a single transformer is trained from scratch on mixed multimodal sequences, with no diffusion model or CLIP encoder in the pipeline. Text-to-image generation, vision-language understanding and causal text-to-video generation or video extension are all performed by predicting the next token. The released post-trained models are split by task: Emu3-Gen for image generation and Emu3-Chat for vision-language understanding.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.18869) · [GitHub](https://github.com/baaivision/Emu3) · [Model card](https://huggingface.co/BAAI/Emu3-Gen)

![Emu3 — Figure 1 (PDF p. 1)](../assets/architectures/emu3.png)

*Figure 1 (PDF p. 1) · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.18869)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I, V → T, I, V · **Interaction:** generation

The vision tokenizer, built on SBER-MoVQGAN with added temporal residual 3D-convolution layers, compresses 4× in time and 8×8 in space and encodes a 512×512 image (or a 4×512×512 clip) into 4,096 tokens from a 32,768-entry codebook. The transformer has 32 layers, hidden size 4096, GQA attention, SwiGLU, RoPE and a 184,622-token vocabulary; text is tokenized with the Qwen tokenizer, and resolution metadata is passed as plain text in the sequence. Vision-token loss is weighted 0.5 during pretraining, and direct preference optimization is applied to the generation model (Emu3-DPO in the paper). Released weights: Emu3-Gen, Emu3-Chat, Emu3-Stage1 (image-pretrained, captioning and 512×512 generation) and the vision tokenizer; the README does not list a released video-generation checkpoint.

**License:** code: Apache-2.0; weights: apache-2.0.

**Variants:** Emu3-Gen; Emu3-Chat; Emu3-Stage1; Emu3-VisionTokenizer.

</details>

<a id="emu3-5"></a>

### Emu3.5

34B decoder-only transformer trained with unified next-token prediction over text and discrete IBQ image tokens, adapted for inference with Discrete Diffusion Adaptation (DiDA) for parallel image-token generation.

Emu3.5 is BAAI's successor to Emu3, described as a native multimodal world model that predicts the next state across vision and language. A single 34B decoder-only transformer is pretrained end-to-end with next-token prediction on about 13 trillion tokens of interleaved vision-language data, mostly frames and transcripts of internet videos, then fine-tuned and trained with large-scale reinforcement learning. It generates interleaved text and images, including text-to-image and any-to-image (X2I) generation and editing, and the paper reports image generation and editing results comparable to Gemini 2.5 Flash Image. For speed, DiDA converts token-by-token image decoding into bidirectional parallel prediction, about 20x faster per image.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26583) · [GitHub](https://github.com/baaivision/Emu3.5) · [Model card](https://huggingface.co/BAAI/Emu3.5-Image)

![Emu3.5 — Figure 3](../assets/architectures/emu3-5.png)

*Figure 3 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26583)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → T, I · **Interaction:** editing

Architecture (paper Section 2.2): 64 layers, hidden size 5,120, GQA with 64 query and 8 key-value heads, QK-Norm, SwiGLU and RoPE; 34.1B parameters; vocabulary of 151,854 Qwen text tokens plus 131,072 vision tokens; 32K context. The IBQ-based tokenizer (16x downsampling, 455M parameters) is trained with SigLIP feature distillation; an optional diffusion-based image decoder takes the same tokens and outputs images at twice the resolution, distilled to 4 steps. DiDA duplicates each image with a noisy copy whose tokens attend bidirectionally within the image and causally to earlier clean tokens (paper Figure 9). The paper also describes a DiT-based video decoder conditioned on generated keyframe tokens; video is not listed as a modality here. The repository recommends the Emu3.5-Image checkpoint for single-image T2I and X2I.

**License:** code: Apache-2.0; weights: Apache-2.0.

**Variants:** Emu3.5; Emu3.5-Image.

</details>

<a id="flat"></a>

### FLAT

Shared VLM encoder with learnable register tokens and nested dropout that maps images and text into one variable-length continuous 1D sequence, jointly trained with contrastive alignment plus a rectified-flow-matching image decoder and an autoregressive text decoder so the same representation drives retrieval and text-to-image/image-to-text generation.

FLAT (Meta AI) is a representation-pretraining framework that jointly optimizes one shared multimodal encoder with downstream text-to-image and image-to-text decoders, so the same continuous representation serves as both a discriminative retrieval embedding and a generative conditioning signal. Images and text are mapped into a unified, variable-length continuous 1D sequence space using register tokens and nested dropout over a prefix length K, trained with combined contrastive and bidirectional generative objectives; a rectified-flow-matching decoder produces images and an autoregressive decoder produces captions. The paper reports competitive cross-modal retrieval alongside a text-to-image GenEval score of 71.1 zero-shot from pretraining (83.1 after task-specific fine-tuning).

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16591) · GitHub: no author-linked repository found

![FLAT — Figure 1 (PDF p. 3)](../assets/architectures/flat.png)

*Figure 1 (PDF p. 3) · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16591)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → T, I · **Interaction:** generation

Paper Figure 1 (PDF p. 3, architecture overview): a shared, LoRA-adapted VLM encoder produces continuous register-token representations for image and caption inputs; nested dropout over prefix-K tokens lets the same encoder output variable-length representations, which are aligned contrastively and also decoded by a rectified-flow-matching image decoder (text-to-image) and a next-token cross-entropy text decoder (image-to-text) from the same 1D sequence space. The paper reports a T2I GenEval score of 71.1 zero-shot from the joint pretraining stage and 83.1 after task-specific fine-tuning, alongside strong retrieval and interpolation/arithmetic properties of the shared representation. No repository or license is disclosed.

</details>

<a id="gill"></a>

### GILL

Frozen LLM adapted with a small trainable visual-input mapping and a learned GILLMapper that translates the LLM's special image-placeholder embeddings into the input space of a frozen Stable Diffusion text encoder, so a pretrained image generator can be conditioned without finetuning it.

GILL (Generating Images with Large Language Models), from CMU, efficiently grounds a frozen autoregressive LLM in visual generation without training or running the image generator during training. A linear layer maps a pretrained visual encoder's image features into the LLM's embedding space so it can process interleaved image-and-text inputs, while on the output side the LLM learns to emit special [IMG] placeholder tokens whose hidden states are mapped, via a learned GILLMapper and an MSE loss against the frozen SD text encoder's own embeddings, into conditioning vectors for an off-the-shelf, frozen Stable Diffusion decoder; a separate retrieval head lets GILL alternatively retrieve rather than generate an image when appropriate.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.17216) · [GitHub](https://github.com/kohjingyu/gill)

![GILL — Figure 2 (PDF p. 3)](../assets/architectures/gill.png)

*Figure 2 (PDF p. 3) · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.17216)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → T, I · **Interaction:** generation

Only the LLM-to-vision caption mapping, the GILLMapper, and retrieval/loss heads are trained; the base LLM, visual encoder and Stable Diffusion model stay frozen throughout (Figure 2: left half 'Learning to Process Images', right half 'Learning to Produce Images'). The image-generation branch is trained with an MSE loss between GILLMapper outputs and the SD text encoder's own embeddings for the same caption, so the generator's own weights never need updating. GILL can interleave retrieved and generated images with generated text in multimodal dialogue (Figure 1, Figure 5). Code and model weights are released on GitHub under Apache-2.0 (per repository license metadata).

**License:** code: Apache-2.0; weights: Apache-2.0.

</details>

<a id="hunyuanimage-3"></a>

### HunyuanImage 3.0

Hunyuan-A13B decoder-only MoE transformer (over 80B total, about 13B active parameters) that predicts text by next-token prediction and denoises 16x-downsampled VAE latents by diffusion within the same sequence.

HunyuanImage 3.0 is Tencent Hunyuan's native multimodal model that unifies understanding and generation in one autoregressive framework; the report describes its image generation module as the largest open-source image generative model to date. Built on the Hunyuan-A13B Mixture-of-Experts language model, it models text tokens autoregressively and image tokens with diffusion prediction in the same sequence, uses a native chain-of-thought schema, and can choose image size and aspect ratio itself through special tokens. The technical report covers data curation, progressive pretraining and post-training (SFT, DPO, MixGRPO, SRPO, ReDA); the initial release is the image generation model, and a later Instruct checkpoint adds reasoning, prompt rewriting and image-to-image generation including editing and multi-image fusion.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.23951) · [GitHub](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/HunyuanImage-3.0) · [Model card](https://huggingface.co/tencent/HunyuanImage-3.0)

![HunyuanImage 3.0 — Figure 3](../assets/architectures/hunyuanimage-3.png)

*Figure 3 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.23951)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → T, I · **Interaction:** editing

The backbone has 64 experts with 8 active per token plus one shared MLP. Generation uses an internal VAE with a 32-channel latent and 16x downsampling, without an extra patchify layer; conditioning images concatenate VAE features and vision-encoder features, projected by a timestep-modulated residual block and a two-layer MLP respectively (paper Section 3.1 and Figure 3). Generalized causal attention keeps text causal while image tokens attend fully within their own image, and a generalized 2D RoPE stays backward compatible with the LLM's 1D RoPE. Editing is documented in the repository for HunyuanImage-3.0-Instruct (README entry dated 2026-01-26), not evaluated in the technical report.

**License:** code: Tencent Hunyuan Community License; weights: Tencent Hunyuan Community License.

**Variants:** HunyuanImage-3.0; HunyuanImage-3.0-Instruct; HunyuanImage-3.0-Instruct-Distil.

</details>

<a id="illume"></a>

### ILLUME

Unified MLLM that reads images as continuous vision-encoder features but generates images as discrete tokens from a semantic vision tokenizer, decoded back to pixels by a diffusion (denoising U-Net) decoder.

ILLUME, from a group including vivo AI Lab, unifies multimodal understanding and generation in one MLLM by using different visual representations for the two directions: input images are embedded as continuous features through a vision encoder and adapter for understanding, while generated images are predicted as discrete tokens from a semantic vision tokenizer whose codebook is trained with both reconstruction and semantic supervision. A diffusion-based decoder (denoising U-Net plus upsampling) converts the predicted discrete tokens back into a higher-resolution image, and a self-enhancing multimodal alignment scheme with progressive training improves data efficiency compared to prior unified models.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06673) · GitHub: no author-linked repository found

![ILLUME — Figure 3](../assets/architectures/illume.png)

*Figure 3 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06673)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → T, I · **Interaction:** editing

The vision tokenizer combines a frozen vision encoder and lookup codebook for discrete tokens with a trainable decoder supervised by cosine and smooth-L1 losses, and a separate denoising U-Net upsamples the reconstruction from a lower resolution to 512x512 (Figure 3b). The MLLM architecture (Figure 3a) shows continuous adapter features for understanding and discrete text/image tokens for generation and editing, including instruction-based image redesign (e.g. style transfer), which is why the card is labeled editing. Three-stage training and a self-enhancing alignment scheme are described in Figures 4-5. No official code or model repository was found at review; ILLUME-plus (2025) is a separate, later model with its own released repository.

</details>

<a id="illume-plus"></a>

### ILLUME+

Unified MLLM over a continuous-input, discrete-output dual vision tokenizer (DualViTok): a semantic branch (QwenViT-based) and a texture-preserving MoVQGAN-style pixel branch feed a coarse-to-fine (semantic tokens then pixel tokens) autoregressive LLM, with an optional diffusion U-Net decoder refining the predicted discrete tokens into images and performing super-resolution.

ILLUME+ is an enhanced version of ILLUME that adds a dual vision tokenizer and a diffusion decoder to close the gap between unified models' understanding, generation and editing abilities. Its DualViTok tokenizer has a semantic branch (a pretrained text-aligned QwenViT encoder, quantized and reconstructed for image-text alignment) and a pixel branch (a MoVQGAN-based encoder that additionally consumes the quantized semantic features to preserve texture), so the same tokenizer captures both deep semantics and fine-grained detail needed for editing. Rather than decoupling input and output representations like the Janus series, ILLUME+ uses continuous pre-quantized features as MLLM input and predicts discrete coarse-to-fine (semantic-then-pixel) tokens as output through one unified LM head, and an optional diffusion U-Net decoder refines those tokens into higher-fidelity, higher-resolution images. The 3B-LLM model is reported competitive with larger unified and specialist models on understanding, generation (up to 1024x1024) and editing benchmarks.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.01934) · [GitHub](https://github.com/illume-unified-mllm/ILLUME_plus) · [Model card](https://huggingface.co/ILLUME-MLLM/illume_plus-qwen2_5-3b-hf)

![ILLUME+ — Figure 3](../assets/architectures/illume-plus.png)

*Figure 3 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.01934)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → T, I · **Interaction:** editing

DualViTok's semantic branch quantizes QwenViT features and is supervised with a cosine-similarity feature-reconstruction loss; the pixel branch follows MoVQGAN and concatenates quantized semantic and pixel features before decoding, with noise injection during training to make token decoding more robust to autoregressive prediction errors (paper Section 3.1, Figure 3a). The diffusion decoder is a denoising U-Net conditioned on the tokenizer's quantized features plus Gaussian noise, used both to raise generation quality above direct token decoding and to perform efficient super-resolution (Figure 3b). The MLLM (Figure 3c) takes continuous adapter-projected semantic and pixel features as visual input for understanding and editing, and autoregressively emits discrete tokens for generation, first semantic then pixel tokens in a chain-of-thought-like ordering with explicit start/end-of-semantic and start/end-of-pixel markers and height/width indicator tokens (Figure 3d). Training is a progressive, resolution-increasing procedure across the tokenizer, MLLM and diffusion decoder. Editing conditions on an input image plus an edit instruction, generating new discrete tokens while relying on the pixel branch for texture consistency in unchanged regions.

**License:** code: Apache-2.0; weights: Apache-2.0.

**Variants:** ILLUME_plus-3B; ILLUME_plus-7B.

</details>

<a id="illume-x"></a>

### ILLUME-X

Unified multimodal transformer with parallel understanding and generation branches (separate FFN/QKV projections per token type) sharing multi-modal self-attention over one sequence of text, VAE and ViT tokens, trained with a specialized attention mask for free-form N-to-M interleaved text-image generation.

ILLUME-X (Harbin Institute of Technology and Huawei Noah's Ark Lab) is a unified multimodal model aimed specifically at free-form, N-to-M interleaved text-image generation — producing arbitrary sequences of text and image outputs, such as illustrated step-by-step instructions or per-object image decompositions, rather than a single fixed-modality output. It combines separate understanding and generation attention branches sharing one multi-modal self-attention over a joint text/VAE/ViT token sequence, trained with a progressive strategy and a specialized attention mask over a curated 100K-sample interleaved dataset. The authors also propose ILScore, an evaluation protocol for cross-modal continuity and per-modality quality in interleaved generation.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30054) · [GitHub](https://github.com/ChonghuinanWang/ILLUME-X)

![ILLUME-X — Figure 2](../assets/architectures/illume-x.png)

*Figure 2 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30054)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → T, I · **Interaction:** generation

Paper Figure 2: each turn's tokens (BOI/VAE/VAE/ViT/ViT/EOI for images, plus text tokens) pass through modality-specific tokenizers (a text tokenizer, a VAE encoder for generation targets, and a ViT encoder for understanding context), then through parallel Understanding and Generation FFN/QKV branches joined by shared multi-modal self-attention; clean image tokens take a cross-entropy loss and noisy image tokens take an MSE (diffusion-style) loss, so the design mixes autoregressive text modeling with diffusion-style image token prediction inside one attention-masked sequence. The paper introduces a 100K-sample interleaved text-image data pipeline (real video-derived sequences plus MLLM-synthesized data) and the ILScore evaluation protocol for interleaved sequences (style transfer, object-level image decomposition, illustrated storytelling). Code is published on GitHub without an explicit open-source license file at review time, so a license is not recorded.

</details>

<a id="internvl-u"></a>

### InternVL-U

InternVL 3.5 MLLM backbone (ViT understanding encoder, unified AR context modeling) extended with a dedicated dual-stream, gated-attention MMDiT visual generation head that denoises VAE image latents by flow matching, conditioned on the MLLM's hidden states via separate projectors and a unified multi-scale 3D RoPE.

InternVL-U is a unified multimodal model built on InternVL 3.5 that argues unified models should not force text and images through one homogeneous pipeline. Its design follows three principles: unified contextual modeling with modality-adaptive generation (a shared autoregressive context space, but a hybrid AR-for-text + flow-matching-for-images generative objective instead of tokenizing everything the same way), structural efficiency through modality-specific modules (a pretrained ViT-based encoder for context, plus a dedicated MMDiT generation head rather than a monolithic transformer), and decoupled visual representations (semantic ViT features for understanding, a separate VAE latent for generation, avoiding a single encoder having to serve both roles). Through three-stage progressive training, InternVL-U inherits InternVL 3.5's understanding and reasoning ability while gaining text-to-image generation and instruction-based editing, and can apply self-reflection reasoning from the MLLM to its generation and editing outputs.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.09877) · [GitHub](https://github.com/OpenGVLab/InternVL-U) · [Model card](https://huggingface.co/InternVL-U/InternVL-U)

![InternVL-U — Figure 3](../assets/architectures/internvl-u.png)

*Figure 3 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.09877)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → T, I · **Interaction:** editing

The visual generation head is a custom dual-stream MMDiT: independent linear projectors (with an added normalization layer on the VLM branch to correct scale mismatch) map the MLLM's context hidden states and the VAE's image latents into a shared conditioning space, then dual-stream MMDiT blocks with disentangled QKVO/FFN parameters per stream interact through joint self-attention, augmented with a sigmoid gating mechanism the paper describes as a first for MMDiT (paper Section 3.1.2, Figure 4). Positional information uses a Unified Multi-Scale RoPE (MSRoPE) applying 3D (temporal, height, width) position embeddings to both generative targets and context visual tokens, plus a resolution-interpolation scheme to avoid tiling artifacts when scaling from low- to high-resolution training. Text generation uses standard next-token-prediction cross-entropy; image generation uses flow matching (a generalized diffusion formulation) over continuous VAE latents, so the loss types differ per modality by design rather than sharing one discretized objective (Section 3.2.1). Editing benefits specifically from the 3D positional scheme for precise spatial reasoning; the paper introduces its own GenEditEvalKit and TextEdit evaluation tooling.

**License:** code: MIT.

**Variants:** InternVL-U.

</details>

<a id="janus"></a>

### Janus

Autoregressive LLM (DeepSeek-LLM 1.3B) with decoupled visual encoders: SigLIP features for understanding and VQ-tokenizer image IDs for generation, predicted by a separate image head.

Janus, from DeepSeek-AI with HKU and Peking University, is an autoregressive framework for unified multimodal understanding and generation. Its key idea is to decouple visual encoding: images for understanding are encoded by a SigLIP semantic encoder, while images for generation are represented as discrete VQ tokenizer IDs, yet both pathways feed a single shared autoregressive transformer. Text is predicted by the LLM's built-in head and image tokens by a separate, newly initialized image head; generated token IDs are decoded to pixels by the VQ decoder. The released 1.3B model handles visual question answering and text-to-image generation at 384×384.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13848) · [GitHub](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/Janus) · [Model card](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/Janus-1.3B)

![Janus — Figure 2](../assets/architectures/janus.png)

*Figure 2 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13848)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → T, I · **Interaction:** generation

Understanding uses SigLIP-Large-Patch16-384; generation uses the LlamaGen VQ tokenizer with a 16,384-entry codebook and 16× downsampling. Understanding and generation adaptors are two-layer MLPs mapping each pathway into the LLM input space (paper Figure 2). Training has three stages: adaptors and image head, unified pretraining, and supervised fine-tuning. The official repository also hosts JanusFlow and Janus-Pro, which have separate cards. The Hugging Face card metadata lists license mit with license_name deepseek; the repository's LICENSE-MODEL is the DeepSeek License Agreement.

**License:** code: MIT; weights: DeepSeek License Agreement.

**Variants:** Janus-1.3B.

</details>

<a id="janus-pro"></a>

### Janus-Pro

Single autoregressive transformer with decoupled visual encoding: SigLIP features for understanding and VQ image tokens, predicted by a separate image head, for generation.

Janus-Pro is DeepSeek's scaled-up successor to Janus, a unified model for multimodal understanding and text-to-image generation. It keeps the Janus architecture, in which one autoregressive language-model transformer reads images through a SigLIP encoder for understanding and writes images as discrete VQ tokens for generation, and changes the training recipe, adds roughly 72 million synthetic aesthetic text-to-image samples, and scales the language model from 1.5B to 7B parameters. The paper reports improved instruction following on GenEval and DPG-Bench and more stable generation for short prompts.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.17811) · [GitHub](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/Janus) · [Model card](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/Janus-Pro-7B)

![Janus-Pro — Figure 3](../assets/architectures/janus-pro.png)

*Figure 3 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.17811)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → T, I · **Interaction:** generation

The architecture is stated to be the same as Janus (paper Figure 3): DeepSeek-LLM base models (1.5B and 7B), a SigLIP-Large-Patch16-384 understanding encoder, and for generation a VQ tokenizer with a 16,384-entry codebook and 16x downsampling, whose code embeddings enter the LLM through a two-layer MLP adaptor; a randomly initialized image head predicts image tokens and an image decoder reconstructs pixels. Changes over Janus are training-only: longer Stage I on ImageNet, Stage II trained directly on dense text-to-image data, a revised Stage III data ratio, and a 1:1 real-to-synthetic data mix. Images are generated at 384x384.

**License:** code: MIT; weights: DeepSeek Model License.

**Variants:** Janus-Pro-1B; Janus-Pro-7B.

</details>

<a id="janusflow"></a>

### JanusFlow

Autoregressive LLM (DeepSeek-LLM 1.3B) that generates text by next-token prediction and images by rectified flow, predicting velocities for SDXL-VAE latents through lightweight ConvNeXt generation encoder/decoder layers.

JanusFlow, from DeepSeek-AI with Peking University, HKU and Tsinghua, integrates rectified flow directly into an autoregressive language model. For understanding, a SigLIP encoder feeds image features to the LLM, which answers by next-token prediction. For generation, the LLM takes the text prompt and a noisy SDXL-VAE latent, processed by a small generation encoder, and a generation decoder turns its outputs into velocity vectors; the latent is updated iteratively from noise until t = 1 and decoded by the VAE. Understanding and generation encoders are decoupled, and a representation-alignment loss ties the LLM's intermediate generation features to the understanding encoder's features. The released 1.3B model works at 384×384.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.07975) · [GitHub](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/Janus) · [Model card](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/JanusFlow-1.3B)

![JanusFlow — Figure 2](../assets/architectures/janusflow.png)

*Figure 2 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.07975)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → T, I · **Interaction:** generation

The generation encoder is a 2×2 patchify layer plus two ConvNeXt blocks and a linear layer; the decoder is two ConvNeXt blocks with pixel-shuffle upsampling, with a long skip connection between them. The paper reports that plain causal attention sufficed, without special attention masks. Classifier-free guidance is applied to the velocity. Training has three stages: adapting the randomly initialized components, unified pretraining and supervised fine-tuning. Released in the same repository as Janus; the Hugging Face card metadata lists license mit with license_name deepseek, and the repository's LICENSE-MODEL is the DeepSeek License Agreement.

**License:** code: MIT; weights: DeepSeek License Agreement.

**Variants:** JanusFlow-1.3B.

</details>

<a id="joyai-image"></a>

### JoyAI-Image

Spatially enhanced MLLM (ViT plus language model) whose final-layer hidden states condition a 16B-parameter dual-stream Multimodal Diffusion Transformer with a modified MRoPE, denoising VAE latents for generation and, for editing, additionally consuming VAE-encoded source-image tokens alongside the MLLM priors.

JoyAI-Image, from JD.com's JD Open Source team, is a unified model for visual understanding, text-to-image generation and instruction-guided image editing built around spatial intelligence. A spatially enhanced MLLM serves both as the understanding engine and as the interface that turns prompts and source images into semantically and spatially grounded conditioning signals, which a 16B-parameter dual-stream MMDiT (following the Qwen-Image style but with MRoPE replacing MSRoPE) consumes to synthesize or edit images through iterative denoising. Training is progressive: the MLLM is first fine-tuned for spatial understanding, the MMDiT is then trained from scratch for generation using MLLM-derived priors, and the whole system is finally optimized for instruction-based editing. The paper emphasizes a bidirectional loop between enhanced spatial understanding, controllable spatial editing (e.g. camera viewpoint changes) and novel-view-assisted reasoning, reporting state-of-the-art or highly competitive results on understanding, generation, long-text rendering and editing benchmarks.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.04128) · [GitHub](https://github.com/jd-opensource/JoyAI-Image) · [Model card](https://huggingface.co/jdopensource/JoyAI-Image-Edit)

![JoyAI-Image — Figure 4](../assets/architectures/joyai-image.png)

*Figure 4 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.04128)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → T, I · **Interaction:** editing

For understanding, a ViT and the MLLM jointly encode image and text tokens for semantic and spatial reasoning; the final-layer MLLM hidden states are extracted as the primary conditioning signal for downstream synthesis and editing (paper Section on MLLM+MMDiT, Figure 4). The 16B-parameter MMDiT is dual-stream (separate gated linear/scale-shift/QK-norm branches per stream with joint self-attention and timestep-embedding conditioning), jointly modeling MLLM-derived multimodal tokens and VAE latent tokens; for generation the sequence is text+understanding tokens plus noise tokens, while for editing it additionally includes VAE-encoded source-image tokens (green tokens in Figure 4) so the diffusion transformer can preserve unedited regions while following the instruction. Camera-viewpoint (novel-view) editing is one of the documented spatial-editing capabilities, generated via a dedicated Blender-based spatial-editing data pipeline (OpenSpatial). The paper documents multimodal understanding, text-to-image generation and instruction-based/spatial image editing; it does not document video or audio modalities.

**License:** code: Apache-2.0; weights: Apache-2.0.

**Variants:** JoyAI-Image; JoyAI-Image-Edit.

</details>

<a id="lavida-o"></a>

### Lavida-O

Elastic Mixture-of-Transformers masked diffusion model that couples an 8B LaViDa understanding branch (SigLIP semantic embeddings) with a smaller 2.4B generation branch operating on compressed VQ-VAE image tokens, jointly denoising masked text and image tokens with modality-aware masking and joint attention limited to early layers.

Lavida-O, from Adobe Research, is a unified masked diffusion model (MDM) that extends prior multimodal MDMs such as MMaDA and Muddit beyond simple low-resolution generation to object grounding, instruction-based image editing and 1024px text-to-image synthesis, all in one framework. It is built on LaViDa, an understanding-only masked diffusion model, and adds image generation through an Elastic Mixture-of-Transformers architecture that keeps the generation branch small and lets text and image tokens interact only in early layers, avoiding the cost of duplicating a full dense model. Lavida-O also introduces planning and iterative self-reflection during generation and editing, letting its own understanding capability critique and refine its outputs. The paper reports state-of-the-art results among masked diffusion models on RefCOCO grounding, GenEval text-to-image generation and ImgEdit editing, beating AR and continuous-diffusion baselines including Qwen2.5-VL and FLUX.1 Kontext-dev with up to 6.8x faster inference.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.19244) · [GitHub](https://github.com/adobe-research/LaVida-O) · [Model card](https://huggingface.co/jacklishufan/LaViDa-O-v1.0)

![Lavida-O — Figure 2](../assets/architectures/lavida-o.png)

*Figure 2 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.19244)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → T, I · **Interaction:** editing

Understanding reuses LaViDa's setup unchanged: a SigLIP vision encoder produces continuous semantic embeddings concatenated with text-prompt embeddings as the condition for masked-diffusion text decoding (paper Section 3.1). Generation represents target images as VQGAN-based discrete VQ tokens compressed 4x by a token-compression module; editing and interleaved generation additionally condition on VQ tokens of the input image (not just its semantic embedding) to preserve low-level detail, concatenating semantic, VQ and prompt condition embeddings before the shared diffusion model predicts the unmasked sequence (Figure 2). The Elastic-MoT design gives the generation branch a smaller hidden size and restricts joint text-image attention to the first M of N layers, so image generation activates only 6.4B of the model's parameters (2.4B generation + 4B from shared early layers) versus 8B for understanding and 10.4B for interleaved tasks (Section 3.1.1). A modality-aware masking scheme routes tokens to the correct branch during parallel decoding using a special expansion token, and universal text conditioning and stratified sampling further improve generation quality (Section 3.1.2, 3.2).

**License:** code: Adobe Research License; weights: Adobe Research License.

**Variants:** LaViDa-O-v1.0.

</details>

<a id="lavit"></a>

### LaVIT

LLaMA-7B trained with next-token prediction over text and dynamic-length discrete visual tokens (EVA-CLIP ViT features selected, merged and vector-quantized), decoded to pixels by a conditional Stable Diffusion U-Net.

LaVIT (Language-VIsion Transformer), from Peking University and Kuaishou Technology, treats images as a foreign language that an LLM can read and write. Its dynamic visual tokenizer passes EVA-CLIP ViT patch features through a token selector that keeps informative patches and a token merger that folds discarded patches into them, then quantizes the retained tokens with a learnable codebook, so the number of visual tokens varies with image content. The LLM is trained with one next image/text token objective, and generated visual tokens are decoded into images by a conditional denoising U-Net. The model handles visual understanding and text-to-image or multimodal-prompt image generation.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.04669) · [GitHub](https://github.com/jy0205/LaVIT) · [Model card](https://huggingface.co/rain1011/LaVIT-7B-v2)

![LaVIT — Figure 2](../assets/architectures/lavit.png)

*Figure 2 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.04669)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → T, I · **Interaction:** generation

The tokenizer uses EVA-CLIP ViT-G/14 as encoder, a 16,384-entry codebook, and 12 transformer blocks for both the token merger and the feature decoder; the pixel-decoding U-Net is initialized from Stable Diffusion v1.5 (paper setup). The paper's default LLM is LLaMA-1 7B; the released weights are rebuilt on Llama-2-7B because LLaMA-1 weights could not be published. The README reports an updated high-resolution pixel decoder (up to 1024×1024, multiple aspect ratios) and LaVIT-v2 with improved aesthetics and prompt alignment. Video-LaVIT, in the same repository, is a separate video model and out of scope. Code: LaVIT Community License Agreement; weights: Hugging Face cards list llama2.

**License:** code: LaVIT Community License Agreement; weights: llama2.

**Variants:** LaVIT-7B-v1 (Llama-2-7B); LaVIT-7B-v2.

</details>

<a id="libra-2"></a>

### Libra-2

Decoupled vision-language architecture (one vision system, one language system) joined by low-rank cross-modal bridges and a switch-attention/switch-FFN mechanism that routes self-modal versus cross-modal computation, with a continuous-space visual tokenizer (a VAE encoder enriched with CLIP features via cross-attention) and UniRoPE positional encoding letting a LLaMA3.2-1B-Instruct-initialized language branch and a from-scratch vision branch share one sequence for causal text generation and bidirectional masked-image generation.

Libra-2 extends the Libra family's decoupled vision-language design from image understanding only (Libra-1) to unified image-to-text understanding and text-to-image generation. Libra keeps one dedicated vision system and one dedicated language system rather than a single shared backbone, connecting them through cross-modal bridges (low-rank projections) and switch attention/switch FFN modules that route computation between self-modal and cross-modal pathways so each modality's own processing is not disturbed by the other. A continuous-space visual tokenizer combines a VAE encoder with CLIP semantic features through cross-attention, and a unified rotary positional encoding (UniRoPE) handles both 2D image and 1D text positions in one sequence; the language branch (initialized from LLaMA3.2-1B-Instruct) is trained with causal attention while the vision branch, trained from scratch, uses masked generation supervision, with the authors reporting that coupling understanding and generation in this decoupled design yields mutual improvements on both.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20382) · [GitHub](https://github.com/YifanXu74/Libra)

![Libra-2 — Fig. 2](../assets/architectures/libra-2.png)

*Fig. 2 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20382)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → T, I · **Interaction:** generation

Paper Figure 2 shows the overall architecture (switch attention/FFN, cross-modal bridges) and the two tokenization paths (hybrid discrete image tokenization and continuous-space tokenization). Libra-2 is 3B parameters total; trained on 200M LAION-COCO/LAION-Aesthetic pairs plus 14M JourneyDB/aesthetic samples. The paper says code "will be available" at the shared Libra GitHub repository, which at review time hosts the original Libra-1 (ICML 2024, understanding-only) implementation under Apache-2.0 and predates the Libra-2 release described here.

</details>

<a id="liquid"></a>

### Liquid

Standard decoder-only LLM over a unified token space combining BPE text tokens and VQVAE discrete image tokens, predicting the next token autoregressively for either modality with no extra vision-specific modules.

Liquid, from ByteDance, HUST and HKU, argues that visual understanding and generation can be added to an LLM without special vision components by simply extending the vocabulary with image codes. Text is BPE-tokenized and images are converted into discrete tokens by a VQVAE image tokenizer; both token streams share one vocabulary that an otherwise-unmodified autoregressive LLM predicts next-token by next-token, so text-to-image generation, image understanding and text generation are all the same task for the model, and existing LLM scaling behavior is shown to transfer to visual generation.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.04332) · [GitHub](https://github.com/FoundationVision/Liquid) · [Model card](https://huggingface.co/Junfeng5/Liquid_V1_7B)

![Liquid — Figure 2](../assets/architectures/liquid.png)

*Figure 2 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.04332)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → T, I · **Interaction:** generation

The pipeline (Figure 2) shows BPE tokenize/detokenize for text and VQVAE tokenize/detokenize for images feeding a single LLM trained with standard next-token prediction over the concatenated vocabulary. The paper studies scaling from 0.5B to 32B parameters and finds mixed multimodal training and pure text-to-image training follow consistent scaling trends, with some trade-off against pure language performance (Figures 3, 5, 6). Liquid-7B-IT (instruction-tuned) checkpoints, training and evaluation code are released on GitHub and Hugging Face under an MIT license.

**License:** code: MIT; weights: MIT.

**Variants:** Liquid-0.5B; Liquid-7B; Liquid-7B-IT; Liquid-32B.

</details>

<a id="llada-o"></a>

### LLaDA-o

Mixture-of-Diffusion (MoD) unified model coupling a discrete masked-diffusion understanding expert (initialized from LLaDA-8B-Instruct) with a continuous rectified-flow diffusion transformer generation expert, sharing one attention backbone with modality-specific QKV/MLP branches and a frozen FLUX VAE for image latents.

LLaDA-o extends the LLaDA masked-diffusion language model into a unified multimodal system by decoupling understanding and generation into two diffusion processes that nonetheless share one attention backbone, rather than bolting a separate diffusion decoder onto a frozen LLM. A discrete masked-diffusion 'understanding expert', initialized from LLaDA-8B-Instruct, handles text and visual tokens for comprehension tasks, while a continuous rectified-flow 'generation expert' -- initialized from the same architecture with newly added time-embedding parameters -- denoises FLUX-VAE image latents for text-to-image generation. The two experts interact only through a shared, efficient attention mechanism (intra-modality bidirectional attention) that keeps cross-modal conditioning global while avoiding the training conflicts the authors report from a single shared token stream.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01068) · [GitHub](https://github.com/ML-GSAI/LLaDA-o)

![LLaDA-o — Figure 2 (PDF p. 4)](../assets/architectures/llada-o.png)

*Figure 2 (PDF p. 4) · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01068)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → T, I · **Interaction:** generation

A data-centric length-adaptation strategy lets the model decode variable-length outputs without architectural changes. The FLUX VAE is kept frozen throughout training. The paper reports 87.04 on the DPG-Bench text-to-image benchmark and releases code.

**License:** code: Apache-2.0.

</details>

<a id="llada2-uni"></a>

### LLaDA2.0-Uni

LLaDA2.0-mini, a 16B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts discrete-diffusion language model, jointly denoises masked text tokens and fully semantic SigLIP-VQ image tokens under one block-wise mask-prediction objective, with a distilled few-step diffusion decoder reconstructing high-fidelity images from the predicted image tokens.

LLaDA2.0-Uni, from Ant Group's inclusionAI, is a unified masked discrete-diffusion language model (dLLM) for multimodal understanding, text-to-image generation and image editing. It argues prior unified masked-diffusion models (MMaDA, Lumina-DiMOO) lag behind AR-based unified models because their reconstruction-focused VQ tokenizers lack semantic richness and over-compress images; LLaDA2.0-Uni instead introduces SigLIP-VQ, a fully semantic discrete tokenizer, so that both text and images can be optimized under one shared block-wise masked diffusion objective inside a 16B MoE dLLM backbone (LLaDA2.0-mini). A dedicated diffusion decoder, optimized through distillation to run in just 8 inference steps, turns the backbone's predicted semantic image tokens into high-fidelity pixels. The paper reports understanding performance competitive with specialized VLMs like Qwen2.5-VL, strong text-to-image generation, flexible single/multi-reference image editing, and native support for interleaved generation and reasoning.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.20796) · [GitHub](https://github.com/inclusionAI/LLaDA2.0-Uni) · [Model card](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/LLaDA2.0-Uni)

![LLaDA2.0-Uni — Figure 4](../assets/architectures/llada2-uni.png)

*Figure 4 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.20796)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → T, I · **Interaction:** editing

The tokenizer, SigLIP-VQ, quantizes SigLIP features into fully semantic discrete tokens rather than reconstruction-optimized codes, which the paper credits for solving the understanding-quality gap that reconstruction-based VQ tokenizers create in prior unified dLLMs (paper Section 2.2, Figure 4). The 16B-parameter LLaDA2.0-mini MoE backbone processes interleaved text and image token sequences (with height/width and other special tokens) under a shared block-level masked diffusion objective, predicting masked positions in parallel rather than autoregressively. Inference efficiency comes from prefix-aware optimizations in the dLLM backbone (for parallel decoding) and few-step distillation in the diffusion decoder (8 steps for image synthesis). Editing is documented for both single- and multi-reference cases, with the original image supplied alongside an edit instruction; the shared discrete representation across modalities also enables interleaved generation and reasoning, evaluated on the authors' own InterGen benchmark.

**License:** code: Apache-2.0; weights: Apache-2.0.

**Variants:** LLaDA2.0-Uni.

</details>

<a id="longcat-next"></a>

### LongCat-Next

LongCat-Flash modality-agnostic Mixture-of-Experts decoder-only backbone that autoregressively predicts a shared sequence of discrete text, vision and audio tokens, with vision handled by dNaViT (a Semantic-and-Aligned-Encoder plus Residual Vector Quantization tokenizer/de-tokenizer pair for arbitrary-resolution images) and audio by an RVQ tokenizer built on a Whisper encoder with a flow-matching refinement decoder.

LongCat-Next, from Meituan's LongCat team, is a native multimodal foundation model built under a proposed Discrete Native Autoregression (DiNA) paradigm: rather than mixing autoregressive text prediction with a separate diffusion or continuous-embedding generator, every modality (text, vision, audio) is represented as discrete tokens in one shared vocabulary, and one modality-agnostic MoE decoder-only backbone (LongCat-Flash) predicts them all next-token-style. Its key vision component, dNaViT, is a paired tokenizer/de-tokenizer that converts images to and from hierarchical discrete tokens at arbitrary resolution using semantic-and-aligned encoders plus residual vector quantization, with up to 28x compression while preserving both semantics (for understanding) and reconstructable detail (for generation). The paper reports LongCat-Next surpassing existing unified frameworks such as Qwen3-Omni, beating specialized understanding models like Qwen3VL-A3B, and competing with FLUX.1-dev on high-fidelity text-to-image generation, particularly text rendering, plus RL post-training for image generation quality.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.27538) · [GitHub](https://github.com/meituan-longcat/LongCat-Next) · [Model card](https://huggingface.co/meituan-longcat/LongCat-Next)

![LongCat-Next — Figure 2](../assets/architectures/longcat-next.png)

*Figure 2 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.27538)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I, A → T, I, A · **Interaction:** generation

dNaViT trains Semantic-and-Aligned Encoders (SAE) for semantically complete visual features, then applies Residual Vector Quantization to build hierarchical discrete tokens combining high-level semantics with fine-grained detail; a paired de-tokenizer reconstructs images at arbitrary resolution from these tokens, and the tokenizer is described as plug-and-play compatible with existing LLMs (paper Section 2.2.5, Figure 3/4). The overall architecture routes text, vision and audio tokens through modality-specific tokenizers into a shared discrete vocabulary consumed by the LongCat-Flash MoE backbone, with modality-specific de-tokenizers on the output side (Figure 2). Audio uses an RVQ-based tokenizer built on a Whisper encoder (12.5 Hz discrete tokens capturing semantic and paralinguistic features) with a decoder plus a flow-matching refinement network for high-fidelity reconstruction, and a segment-level text-audio alignment scheme (following Moshi) supports both parallel and serial text-guided speech generation (Section 2.2, Figure 6-7). Within the DiNA framework, visual understanding and generation are treated as the same predictive process differing only in conditioning direction (image tokens conditioning text output vs. text tokens conditioning image output). The paper's evaluation covers image-to-text understanding and text-to-image generation plus speech generation; it does not document instruction-based image editing, and the authors explicitly note extending to any-to-any interleaved generation as future work.

**License:** code: MIT; weights: MIT.

**Variants:** LongCat-Next.

</details>

<a id="lumina-dimoo"></a>

### Lumina-DiMOO

LLaDA-Base masked discrete-diffusion language model extended with an 8,192-entry aMUSEd-VQ image-token vocabulary, jointly denoising masked text and image tokens by parallel prediction-sampling-remasking.

Lumina-DiMOO, from the Lumina/Alpha-VLLM team, is an open unified model that uses fully discrete diffusion rather than autoregression or hybrid AR-diffusion for both text and image tokens. Starting from the pretrained LLaDA-Base diffusion LLM, it extends the vocabulary with discrete image tokens from an aMUSEd-VQ tokenizer and trains a single masked-token denoising objective shared across modalities, which the paper reports yields much faster sampling (32x over the autoregressive Lumina-mGPT 2.0, plus a further 2x from a training-free Max-Logit Cache) than prior unified paradigms. It supports text-to-image generation at arbitrary and high resolution and a range of image-to-image tasks (editing, inpainting, subject-driven and controllable generation, style transfer) alongside image understanding, and reports first place on the open-source UniGenBench leaderboard at the time of the report.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.06308) · [GitHub](https://github.com/Alpha-VLLM/Lumina-DiMOO) · [Model card](https://huggingface.co/Alpha-VLLM/Lumina-DiMOO)

![Lumina-DiMOO — Figure 3](../assets/architectures/lumina-dimoo.png)

*Figure 3 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.06308)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I → T, I · **Interaction:** editing

The image tokenizer is aMUSEd-VQ (16x16 downsampling, 8,192-entry codebook) chosen over SBER-MoVQGAN for shorter token sequences at high resolution (paper Section 3.1). The base language model is LLaDA-Base, used without structural modification; only the new visual and special tokens (e.g. <IMAGE>/</IMAGE>) require learning, while LLaDA's 126,345 text tokens are kept (Section 3.2). Training masks a random fraction of a mixed text-image token sequence and predicts the masked positions in parallel via cross-entropy (paper Figure 3a); inference starts from fully masked tokens and iteratively predicts, samples and remasks over T steps (Figure 3b). Editing and other image-to-image tasks condition on encoded input-image tokens alongside the text instruction, and a zero-shot inpainting capability is extended into an interactive retouching workflow.

**License:** code: Apache-2.0; weights: Apache-2.0.

**Variants:** Lumina-DiMOO.

</details>

<a id="lwm"></a>

### LWM

Single autoregressive transformer over BPE text tokens and VQGAN discrete image/video tokens, trained on long multimodal sequences with blockwise RingAttention to reach million-token context for joint text, image and video understanding and generation.

LWM (Large World Model), from UC Berkeley, is a general-purpose autoregressive transformer trained on long video-and-language sequences to build a 'world model' with up to a 1M-token context. Every modality is discretized to a shared vocabulary: text uses a BPE tokenizer and each video frame (or standalone image) is tokenized into 256 discrete tokens by a VQGAN, so the same next-token-prediction transformer can answer long-document and long-video questions, and, run in the other direction, generate images and videos from text prompts.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.08268) · [GitHub](https://github.com/LargeWorldModel/LWM)

![LWM — Figure 3](../assets/architectures/lwm.png)

*Figure 3 · [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.08268)*

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Input → output:** T, I, V → T, I, V · **Interaction:** generation

Training uses RingAttention over progressively longer curated sequences in two stages (text-only then video-text), scaling context length up to roughly one million tokens with high model-flops utilization (Figures 3-4, 8). Image and video generation from text are demonstrated qualitatively (Figure 7), though the paper's primary contribution and evaluation emphasis is long-context text and video understanding (needle retrieval, long-video QA, Figures 2, 5-6) rather than image-generation benchmarks. Code and checkpoints (LWM-Text, LWM, LWM-Chat variants up to 1M context) are released on GitHub under Apache-2.0.

**License:** code: Apache-2.0; weights: Apache-2.0.

**Variants:** LWM-Text; LWM-Text-Chat; LWM; LWM-Chat; LWM-1M; LWM-Chat-1M.

</details>

<a id="mammothmoda2"></a>

### MammothModa2
